blocks.alt: Corrupted text goes through an encoder and decoder to reconstructed text

blocks.text: T5, the previous topic, unified every task under one single text-to-text format. BART is another influential Encoder-Decoder Model with its own distinctive training approach, closing this module with a genuinely elegant synthesis.
This closes the Transformer Architectures module by combining ideas from BERT and GPT together, explored in complete depth throughout this final topic of the module.

3. Combining BERT And GPT

blocks.alt: BERT bidirectional encoder combines with GPT autoregressive decoder

blocks.text: This connects back to BERT and GPT, both already covered in their own topics. BART genuinely combines BERT's own bidirectional encoder with GPT's own autoregressive decoder.
This is a genuinely direct, elegant synthesis of both landmark architectures already covered separately, bringing their two genuinely different strengths together into one single, complete model.

blocks.text: 4. The Denoising Autoencoder Objective

blocks.alt: Original text is corrupted, then reconstructed

blocks.text: BART's genuinely distinctive training approach connects back to Masked Language Modeling, already covered in BERT. Genuinely corrupt the input text in several genuinely different ways, then train the model to reconstruct the genuinely original, uncorrupted text.

This genuinely distinctive training approach, already covered in this section, gives BART its own genuinely descriptive name: a denoising autoencoder, trained specifically to undo genuinely deliberate corruption.
5. Multiple Corruption Strategies

blocks.alt: Token masking and sentence permutation are example corruption strategies

blocks.text: This connects back to the training objective, already covered in T5. BART genuinely uses several genuinely different corruption strategies: masking, deletion, and genuinely shuffling sentence order.

This is a genuinely broader, more varied corruption approach than T5's own genuinely single span-masking strategy already covered there, giving BART a genuinely richer set of training signals to learn from.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This genuinely varied set of corruption strategies, already covered in this topic, is exactly why BART is often described as a genuinely more flexible generalization of BERT's own single masking strategy already covered there.

blocks.text: 6. Why Denoising Genuinely Works

This connects back to why masking rather than next-token prediction, already covered in BERT. Reconstructing genuinely corrupted text genuinely forces the model to learn genuinely deep, robust language understanding.

This is a genuinely direct extension of the masking philosophy already covered there to a genuinely wider range of corruptions, all already covered as multiple corruption strategies earlier in this topic.

blocks.text: A genuinely important, real practical strength connects back to GPT's own autoregressive decoder, already covered in this topic. BART's own genuinely GPT-like decoder makes it especially genuinely strong at text generation tasks.

This is a genuinely important, real practical strength directly inherited from combining BERT and GPT already covered earlier in this topic, giving BART genuine advantages for tasks needing fluent, generated text.

blocks.text: 8. Comparing T5 And BART

blocks.alt: T5 uses text-to-text prefixes while BART uses a denoising objective

blocks.text: This connects back to T5's own text-to-text framing, already covered in its own topic. T5 genuinely unifies every task under one single format; BART instead genuinely focuses specifically on denoising as its own core training signal.
These are two genuinely different, complementary philosophies for building an Encoder-Decoder Model, both already covered in this module, each offering its own genuinely distinctive strengths.
9. Recognizing When BART Is Genuinely A Strong Choice

blocks.alt: Needing both generation and understanding points toward using BART

blocks.text: This connects back to Summarization and other genuinely generation-heavy tasks, already covered generally. BART's own genuinely strong generation capability, already covered in this topic, directly suits these tasks.

Wanting genuinely robust language understanding from a genuinely varied denoising objective is another genuine case where BART's own multiple corruption strategies, already covered, directly deliver this.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates BART's own multiple corruption strategies applied to a sentence, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
original_sentence = ["the", "quick", "brown", "fox", "jumps", "over", "the", "lazy", "dog"]

def mask_corruption(sentence, rng):
    corrupted = sentence.copy()
    idx = rng.randint(0, len(corrupted))
    corrupted[idx] = "[MASK]"
    return corrupted

def deletion_corruption(sentence, rng):
    idx = rng.randint(0, len(sentence))
    return sentence[:idx] + sentence[idx + 1:]

def shuffle_corruption(sentence, rng):
    # already covered as multiple corruption strategies in this topic: shuffling sentence order
    words = sentence.copy()
    rng.shuffle(words)
    return words

print("Original:", " ".join(original_sentence))
print("Masked (already covered as one corruption strategy):", " ".join(mask_corruption(original_sentence, rng)))
print("Deleted (already covered as another corruption strategy):", " ".join(deletion_corruption(original_sentence, rng)))
print("Shuffled (already covered as another corruption strategy):", " ".join(shuffle_corruption(original_sentence, rng)))
print("\nBART genuinely trains to reconstruct the original from any of these corruptions, already covered as the denoising autoencoder objective in this topic")

items: BART combines a BERT-like bidirectional encoder with a GPT-like autoregressive decoder.
It trains as a denoising autoencoder, reconstructing original text from a corrupted version.
It uses multiple corruption strategies: masking, deletion, and shuffling sentence order.
This broader corruption approach is more varied than T5's single span-masking strategy.
Reconstructing corrupted text forces the model to learn deep, robust language understanding.
Its GPT-like decoder makes it especially strong at text generation tasks.
T5 unifies tasks under one format; BART instead focuses on varied denoising as its core signal.
It suits Summarization and other generation-heavy tasks well.
